_readme: Errand playbooks for the text channel (D-25). ONE file, no code per type: adding a type is a new entry here plus its eval cases.

Each entry: id, name, match (rule words that recognise the type in an errand's own words), typical_questions, sources (which sources an answer may use, in order), guidance (what the model is told when it recognises the type), asks (what HO:RA asks before the booking summary), supporter_notes (fixed lines added to the task the supporter reads), summary_lines (fixed lines shown in the summary), limits (what HO:RA never does or promises for this type), evals.

Recognition by rule: the FIRST entry (in file order) whose match words appear, and whose unless words do not, wins. Companionship comes first (company with the customer in a public place; the scope rules decline the rest before any playbook is read), then gifts: buying something for someone ('send flowers to my mom', 'get a cake for my friend') is a gift; friend is only for picking up or dropping off an existing item. Then the specific types (check, packages, small services) before the generic ones (food, groceries). The model names the type itself in discovery answers.

asks[].skip_if: a Go regexp on the person's words; when it matches, the question is not asked (already answered). asks[].answer: 'redraft' (the answer is errand words: re-parsed, so a time or address lands in the booking) or 'note' (kept as a supporter note with asks[].note as its prefix). All remaining questions go out in ONE message; any 'redraft' among them makes the answer a redraft.

sources: places_facts (Google's structured fields, rendered by rule), places_summary (Google's editorial summary only, read by the model, checked by rule; Google's AI review / generative summaries are never used, their attribution does not fit a text), web (one Anthropic web search of the place's own website, used only when the editorial summary names nothing), none.

evals[].kind: 'asks' (rule only: which asks fire for these words; run by go test), 'discover' (the discovery model reads a message with options open; run by agenttest -playbooks), 'answer' (the answer path on fixture facts from eval_places; run by agenttest -playbooks). Grades: no invented facts, no booking, no HO:RA price.
Nothing here is a source of facts about a place. Fixture places in eval_places are invented and exist only for the evals.

discover evals: hora_line 'pizza' / 'laundry' / 'levain' stand for the options answer the runner renders from cmd/agenttest/discovery.json's fixtures (RenderDiscovery). earlier: the search's earlier words. answer evals: place2 adds a second option (compare).

Scope rules (2026-11-10): what HO:RA does and does not do about people and homes. Rules are a fast path; Sonnet (LLM_SMALL_MODEL) decides when no rule does. Every inbound message the person can still act on is checked, ahead of discovery, drafting and relaying to a supporter (channel/scope.go).

Order: refusals (file order; the first whose match words appear and whose unless words do not), then allow (a plainly allowed shape: match AND with AND NOT unless), then sensitive (no sensitive word at all = an everyday errand, allowed). Anything left goes to the model, which answers 'allow' or a refusal id. A model error allows (logged): the clear refusals are the rules'.
A refusal sends its fixed reply and never drafts. alert: true also tells ops at once as urgent (supporter safety); the person gets only the reply.
people and homes: what IS allowed, as plain sentences, given to the model with every playbook and to the scope check; each refusal's rule sentence too.

home_entry: a supporter going inside a home. Its ask is put before the summary (with the type's own) unless the words say who is there or how to get in; its note goes on the task, its line on the summary.
evals: want is 'allow' or a refusal id ('a|b': either). go test runs the rules on them and every case through the router; agenttest -scope runs rules then the model.
people: Companionship in PUBLIC places only: a walk, grabbing a coffee, keeping the customer company at a park, a café, a library or a museum. The meeting point must be a public place. No bars or clubs, no alcohol.
Companionship is with the customer themselves. Accompanying anyone else (a parent, grandparent, friend, partner) is not offered for now.
Picking up items from, or dropping items off with, someone else (a friend, a neighbour, family) is allowed: items only, handed to the adult named.
homes: Entering the customer's home is allowed only for a specific errand (pick up the laundry bag, put groceries away), and only that errand.
Inside a home, the customer or an adult they name is there, or the customer gives clear access instructions (a doorman, a lockbox, "the bag is by the door"). A supporter is never alone with a child.
